entries.content: They made] See the Note on Verſ 1.

entries.title: Exodus 33:1
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: SEE the Note on Chap. 32.7.

entries.title: Exodus 33:3
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: I will not go up] ſc. By thoſe viſible ſigns of my gratious preſence, (Hoſ. 9.11.) as heretofore.

entries.title: Exodus 33:4
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: They mourned] As good cauſ they had: for wo bee unto thee when I depart from thee.

entries.title: Exodus 33:5
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: And conſume thee] God's threatnings are cordial, but conditional. Minatur Deus ut non puniat. Furie is not in mee, Iſa. 27.4. Hee puniſheth not till there bee no other remedie. 2 Chron. 36.16. as the bee ſtin'gs not till provoked.

entries.title: Exodus 33:6
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Stript themſelvs] As in a daie of reſtraint.

entries.title: Exodus 33:7
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Afar off from the camp] In token of God's deep diſpleaſure, and departure from them.

entries.title: Exodus 33:8
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: And looked after Moſes] To ſee what ſucceſs, what accepta[ilegible]: as David looked up after his praier, to ſee how it ſped. Pſalm. 5.3.

entries.title: Exodus 33:10
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Roſe up and worſhipped] Though obnoxious; they would not deſpair of mercie. See 1 Sam. 12.20, 21, 22.

entries.title: Exodus 33:12
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: See, thou ſaieſt unto mee] See (ſaith one) how Moſes here encroacheth upon God. (Mr. Bu[ilegible]r.) God had don much for him, hee muſt have more. Verſ 13. Shew mee now thy waie, &c. This God grant's him. Verſ 14. This ſerv's not the turn, hee muſt have more yet. Verſ 16. Well, hee hath it. Verſ 17. Is hee ſaid? No, hee muſt yet have more. Verſ 18. I beſeech thee ſhew mee thy glorie. It's don. Verſ 19. Is hee ſatisfied yet? No. Chap. 34.9. God muſt pardon the ſin of his people too; and take them and him for his inheritance: This fruit of his favor hee muſt needs bee intreated to add to the reſt, &c.

entries.title: Exodus 33:13
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: That I may know thee] Moſes knew more of God then anie man; hee was but newly com down from the Mount, and at the Tabernacle door God ſpake with Moſes face to face, as a man ſpeaketh unto his friend. Verſ 11. The more a man know's of God, the more deſirous hee is to know him.

entries.title: Exodus 33:14
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: I will give thee reſt] Full content of minde in the ſenſ of my preſence, and light of my countenance.

entries.title: Exodus 33:15
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: If thy preſence go not with mee] What is it to have the air without light? What was all Mordecai's honor to him, when the King frowned upon him?

entries.title: Exodus 33:16
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: So ſhall wee bee ſeparated] Heb. Marvellouſly ſeparated. The ſeparation of the Saints is a wonderful ſeparation. See Deut. 4.7. Iſa. 20.6. where Judea is for this cauſ called an Iſle.

entries.title: Exodus 33:17
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: I know thee by name] As Princes do their favorites, who eaſily forget others, as Saul did David. (1 Sam. 17.55.)

entries.title: Exodus 33:18
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Shew mee thy glorie] None ever knew God's glorie; our cockle-ſhell can never comprehend this ſea, yet it may bee apprehended that it is incomprehenſible.

entries.title: Exodus 33:19
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: I will make all my goodneſs] My glorious goodneſs. Thus Moſes may have what hee will of God. The King is not hee that can do anie thing againſt you, ſaid Zedekiah to his Courtiers. Jer. 38.5.

entries.title: Exodus 33:20
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Thou canſt not ſee my face] Otherwiſe then in his words and works. Rom. 1.20. As wee cannot ſee the Sun in rota, in the circle, but in the beams. (Rab. Maimon.) Som have been Mercabah velo harocheb (as the Hebrew's ſpeak) the charret in which God rode, but not the rider in it: they ſaw ſom created Image, Glorie, whereby hee teſtified his more immediate preſence, but not himſelf. [No man ſhall ſee mee and live] But bee oppreſt and ſwallowed up with Majeſtie: as the ſight of the eie is dazled with the ſun; or a cryſtal-glaſs broken with the fire.

entries.title: Exodus 34:1
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: NOt without a tincture of paſſionate infirmitie, (Dr. Hall.) as ſom conceiv. Hee that was the meekeſt upon earth (ſaith one) in a ſudden indignation abandon's that which hee would in cold blood have held faſter then his life. But Auſtin crie's out, O ira Prophetica, & animus non perturbatus, ſed illuminatus!

entries.title: Exodus 34:2
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: In the morning] A ſign of mercie. Pſalm 90.14. and 30.6. and 5.4.

entries.title: Exodus 34:3
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Neither let anie man bee ſeen] See the Note on Exod. 19.12.

entries.title: Exodus 34:4
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: And hee hewed two Tables] Moſes hewed them. The firſt Tables were hewen out of the Saphir of the Throne of God's Glorie, ſaie the Jewiſh Doctors.

entries.title: Exodus 34:6
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: The Lord, the Lord God, &c] Theſe glorious titles and attributes are thoſe back-parts of God. Chap. 33.23. None can ſee more then theſe and live: and wee need ſee no more then theſe, that wee may live. [Long-ſuffering] Heb. Wide of noſtrils; not apt to ſnuff at ſmall matters, but bearing with men's evil manners. This Averroës the Atheïſt made uſe of as an argument againſt the Providence of God, and to prove that hee medleth with nothing below the Moon, becauſ of his ſlowneſs to anger. [In goodneſs and truth] God's goodneſs, though great, yet here and elſwhere it go's bounded with his truth.

entries.title: Exodus 34:7
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Forgiving iniquitie, tranſgreſſion, and ſin] i. e. All ſorts of ſins. 'Tis natural to him, as here. None like him for this. Micah 7.18. It is the comfort of Saints, that they have to do with a forgiving God. Neh. 9.31. that can multiplie pardons, (Nun rabbathi Maſor.) as they multiplie ſins. Iſa. 55.7. [Keeping mercie for thouſands] The Hebrew word here rendred Keeping, is written with a greaten letter then ordinarie, to note the extraordinarie greatneſs of God's promiſe to his people and their poſteritie▪ Pſalm 25.10. [Clear the guiltie] This laſt letter in God's Name muſt ſtill bee remembred.

entries.title: Exodus 34:8
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: And Moſes made haſte] It was time for him. The more anie man ſee's of God, the lower hee fall's in his own eies: as hee that hath looked intently upon the ſun, ſee's little when hee look's down again.

entries.title: Exodus 34:9
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Let my Lord, I praie thee] See the Note on Cha. 33 12.

entries.title: Exodus 34:10
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Behold, I make a covenant] i. e. I re-eſtabliſh it with this back-ſliding people. God receiveth returning ſinners with much ſweetneſs: Hee reteineth not his anger for ever, becauſ mercie pleaſeth him. His mercie (to us) is greater then his juſtice, though in themſelvs they are equal, yea, the ſame. [I will do marvels] See this fulfilled and recorded. Joſh. 10.12, 13.

entries.title: Exodus 34:11
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Obſerv thou] This is the condition of the covenant on man's part to bee performed. With others God make's a ſingle covenant onely, that they ſhall obſerv that which hee command's them: but with his Elect hee make's a double covenant; to perform both parts to work all their works in them, and for them, to put his fear into their hearts, and to cauſ them to keep his Commandements.

entries.title: Exodus 34:12
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: With the inhabitants] They were devoted to deſtruction, as having filled the land from one end to another with their uncleanneſs. Ezra 9.11.

entries.title: Exodus 34:13
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Break their images] The Popiſh Hiſtorians have blurred and blaſted thoſe zealous Emperors, Zeno and others, that were Iconomachi and Iconoclaſtai, as Sacrilegious. Berne was the firſt Town that after the Reformation was purged of Images; which Auguſtin ſaith cannot bee placed in Churches Sine praeſentiſſimo idololatriae periculo: (Aug. in Pſal. 114.) without extreme danger of Idolatrie. Ephiphanius ſaith, It is utterly unlawful and abominable, to ſet up Images in the Churches of Chriſtians. Irenaeus reproveth the Gnoſticks, for that they carried about the picture of Chriſt in Pilate's time, after his own proportion: uſing alſo, for declaration of their affection toward it, to ſet garlands upon the head of it.

entries.title: Exodus 34:14
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: No other God] In the Hebrew word Acher rendred Other, there is a great R. to ſhew the greatneſs of the ſin of ſerving anie other God.

entries.title: Exodus 34:15
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: And one call thee] Anie one of the Idolatrous root, if hee do but hold up his finger to thee, thou wilt eaſily follow him. Cereus in vitium flecii. (Horat.)

entries.title: Exodus 34:16
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: And they make thy ſons] Satan ſtill work's upon Adam by Eve. Omnes haereſes ex gyneciis. It is the guiſ of Hereticks to abuſe the help of women to ſpread their poiſonful opinions. Satan per coſtam, tanquam per ſcalam ad cor aſſcendit. (Greg.) Satan climbe's up by the rib to the heart.

entries.title: Exodus 34:17
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: No molten gods] As the golden calf was. Goodlie gods that are molten: Olim truncus eram. (Horat.)

entries.title: Exodus 34:18
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: In the moneth Abi[ilegible]] So called from the new fruits, or ears of corn, then firſt appearing. See Exod. 12.1. & 13.4. God here repeteth diverſ Laws; It was a token of reconciliation to the people after their Apoſtacie, in that hee treat's with them again (after their repentance) about his ſolemn worſhips. So, for a teſtimonie of his reconciliation to Peter after his foul fall, hee ſet's him a work in the Miniſterie. John 21.15. So hee commendeth his Sponſ[ilegible]a[ilegible]reſh, after her drowſie decaies, everie whit as amiable as ſhee was before he[ilegible] fall. Cant. 6.5. with Chap. 5.10, 11, &c.

entries.title: Exodus 34:21
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: In earing-time and harveſt] Though moſt buſie times, you may not make bold with God.

entries.title: Exodus 34:24
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Neither ſhall anie man deſire] A wonderful providence, ſith Judea was compaſſed about with ſuch warlike adverſaries; that they ſhould not watch and catch at ſuch opportunities. Pompey beſieging Jeruſalem, made his ſtrongeſt batteries on the Sabbath-daie (whereon hee knew the ſuperſtitious Jews would not make their defence) and took it. (Dio. Caſſ.)

entries.title: Exodus 34:27
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: I have made a covenant] Wee alſo have the Covenant, the Seals, Miniſters, &c. But, alas! are not theſe bleſſings amongſt us as the Ark was amongſt the Philiſtims, rather as priſoners then as privileges? rather in testimonium & ruinam quàm in ſalutem? Rather for our ruine, then reformation.

entries.title: Exodus 34:28
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Fortie daies and fortie nights] Moſes, Elias, and Chriſt, (thoſe three great Fathers) met glorious in Mount Tahor. Abſtinence merit's not; but prepare's the beſt for good duties. [Hee wrote] That is, (Weemſ Exer.) God wrote, as ſom will have it.

entries.title: Exodus 34:29
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: The skin of his face ſhone] God hereby aſſuring the people, that hee had inwardly inlightned him for their better inſtruction.

entries.title: Exodus 34:30
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: And they were afraid] This was another manner of Brightneſs and Majeſtie then that which ſate in the eies of Auguſtus and of Tamerlan; whoſe eies ſo ſhone, as that a man could hardly endure to behold them without cloſing of his own: and manie in talking with them, and often beholding of them became dumb: which cauſſed them oft-times with a comlie modeſtie to abſtein from looking too earneſtly upon ſuch as ſpake unto them, (Turk. hiſt[ilegible] fol. 236.) or diſcourſed with them.

entries.title: Exodus 34:33
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Hee put a veil on his face] And had more glorie by his veil, then by his face. How far are thoſe ſpirits from this Chriſtian modeſtie, which care onely to bee ſeen, and wiſh onely to dazle others eies with admiration, not caring for unknown riches? This veil ſignified the Laws obſcuritie, and our infidelitie.

entries.title: Exodus 34:34
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: But when Moſes went in] Hypocrites on the contrarie ſhew their beſt to men, their worſt to God; God ſee's both their veil; and their face; and I know not whether hee hate's more their veil of diſſimulation, or face of wickedneſs.

entries.title: Exodus 35:1
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content:
HEE often go's over the ſame things, as the knife doth the whetſtone. Good things muſt bee repeted, ſicut in acuendo. 'Tis Moſes his own metaphor. Deut. 6.7.

Ver. Six daies ſhall work bee don] This dutie is ſo oft inculcated, to ſhew the neceſſitie, excellencie, difficultie of well doing it.

Ver. Yee ſhall kindle no fire] ſc. For the furtherance of the work of the Tabernacle: or at leaſt, that is not of abſolute neceſſitie. It might alſo ſignifie, that in the kingdom of heaven wee ſhall bee ſet free from all the fire and ſcorching heat of affliction.

entries.title: Exodus 35:22
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: And brought bracelets] Glad they had anie thing of price to dedicate to God, and to ſeal up their thankfulneſs for this re-admittance into his love and favor. See the Note on Matth. 9.10. Nazianzen put this price upon his Athenian learning (wherein hee was verie famous) that hee had ſomthing of value, to part with for Chriſt.

entries.title: Exodus 35:32
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: And to deviſe curious works] This alſo cometh forth from the Lord of Hoſts, (Lib. 23.) who is wonderful in counſel, and excellent in working. Iſa. 28.29. Plinie make's mention of ſom famous Painters, whoſe rare pieces were Oppidorum opibus venditae: Sold for ſo manie Towns-wealth. A certain artificer ſet a watch-clock upon a ring that Charls the Fifth wore upon his finger. (Sphinx philoſ. pag. 90.) King Ferdinand ſent to Solyman the Turk, for a preſent, a wonderful globe of ſilver, of moſt rare and curious device; daily expreſſing the hourly paſſing of the Time, the motions of the Planets, (Turk. Hiſt. fol. 713.) the change and full of the Moon; lively exepreſſing the wonderful converſions of the Celeſtial frame. To which, I may well add that admirable invention of Printing, a ſpecial bleſſing of God to mankinde.

entries.title: Exodus 36:2
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: GOd qualified them, M[ilegible]ſes called them. Miniſters alſo muſt have an outward calling too. (See Acts 13.1, 2, 3.) Heb. 5.4. and bee ſent ere they preach. Rom. 10.15. And whereas 1 Cor. 14.31. It is ſaid, Yee may all prophecie, the meaning is, All yee that are Prophets, may. But are all Prophets? 1 Cor. 12.29.

entries.title: Exodus 36:7
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: And too much] Thus in outward ordinances of ſervice, and for the making of a worldlie ſanctuarie. Heb. 9.1. they could do and over-do. So John 6.28. They ſaid unto him, What ſhall wee do that wee may work the works of God? Men would fain have heaven as a purchaſe. I would ſwim through a ſea of brimſtone (ſaid one) that I might com to heaven at laſt. But what ſaid our Saviour to thoſe queſtioniſts. John 6? This is the work of God that yee believ on him whom hee hath ſent. And what ſaid Luther, Walk in the Heaven of the Promiſs, but in the Earth of the Law; that in reſpect of Believing, this of Working? Manie poor ſouls can think of nothing but working themſelvs to life. Do wee muſt all righteouſneſs, but reſt in none but Chriſt's.

entries.title: Exodus 36:8
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content:
And everie wiſe-hearted man] Let no man look upon this and the following Chapter, as an idle repetition; nor ſaie as one ſaid once, Did wee not know that all Scripture was divinely inſpired, wee ſhould bee readie to ſa[ilegible]e, Quandoque bonus dormitat Homerus. But know that here is ſee forth a Table, Index, or Inventorie, of what Moſes and the workmen did in obedience to God's command, for everie particular about the Sanctuarie. This Inventorie was taken by Ithamar, at the commandement of Moſes, Et ſic in archivum Eccleſiae relatum, and ſo laid up in the charter-houſ of the Church, for the uſe of poſteritie.

See the Notes on Exod. 26. and conſider that ſaying of an antient. (Proſper. Epiſt. ad Auguſtin.) Neceſſarium & utile est etiam quae ſcripta ſunt ſcribere, nè leve exiſtimetur quod non frequenter arguitur.

entries.title: Exodus 40:36
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: THe Jews conceiv that this Cloud that led Iſraël through the wilderneſs, levelled mountains, raiſed vallies, and laid all aflat: that it burnt up buſhes, and ſmoothed rocks, and made all plain, &c. See Luke 3.5, Iſa. 4.5.
